content.title: What are DriverManager & Connection?
content.description: DriverManager is a JDBC utility class responsible for managing database drivers and establishing database connections, while Connection represents an active session between a Java application and a database.

content.content: Before executing SQL queries, a Java application must establish communication with the database. The DriverManager class locates an appropriate JDBC driver and creates a Connection object. This connection acts as a communication channel through which SQL statements are sent and results are received.

content.title: Why are DriverManager & Connection Important?
content.content: Without DriverManager and Connection, a Java application cannot communicate with a relational database. Every JDBC operation begins with establishing a valid database connection.
Role of DriverManager
The DriverManager class manages registered JDBC drivers and selects the appropriate driver based on the database URL supplied by the application.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: DriverManager automatically chooses the correct JDBC driver by examining the database URL.

content.content: Creating a Connection
The most commonly used method is DriverManager.getConnection(), which returns a Connection object representing an active session with the database.
Connection URL
The JDBC URL identifies the database type, server, port, and database name required for establishing a connection.

content.title: JDBC URL Example
content.content: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/studentdb connects to the MySQL database named 'studentdb' running on localhost at port 3306.
Connection Interface
The Connection interface provides methods for executing SQL statements, managing transactions, creating prepared statements, and closing the database connection.

content.title: Creating a Statement
content.code:
Connection con = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password);
Statement stmt = con.createStatement();

content.content: Closing the Connection
Closing database resources after use is important to avoid memory leaks and unnecessary database connections.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Telephone Operator
content.content: Think of DriverManager as a telephone operator who connects your call to the correct department. Once connected, the phone line itself is the Connection through which both parties communicate.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: DriverManager, Connection, JDBC URL, getConnection(), createStatement(), prepareStatement(), transactions, commit(), rollback(), auto-commit mode, and connection pooling are frequently asked Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Why should connections always be closed?
items.answer: Open connections consume database resources and may eventually exhaust the connection limit.

items.question: Can one Connection object communicate with multiple databases?
items.answer: No. Each Connection object is associated with a single database session.

items.question: Should credentials be hardcoded in production code?
items.answer: No. Database credentials should be stored securely using configuration files or environment variables.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: DriverManager establishes database connections, while the Connection object represents the active communication channel between Java and the database.
